claim: Mukhtar et al. (Heliyon 2023) compare polynomial regression (PR) and a Kriging-based surrogate model class for CFD-based ventilation-rate design optimization of an underground shelter, but use exactly one optimizer throughout (Shifted Hammersley Sampling), explicitly declining to run the two other available optimizers (MOGA, NLPQL) -- failing the requirement that the optimizer axis be varied and crossed with surrogate class.
stance_target: Mukhtar 2023 as a candidate KILL or near-miss of N6
scope_conditions: CFD-based engineering design optimization, ANSYS Design Explorer, 2023
quoted_support: there are three optimisation methods available in ANSYS Design Explorer, i.e. Shifted Hammersly Sampling (SHS), Multi-objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) and Non-linear Programming by Quadratic Lagrangian (NLPQL) ... In the current study, we have decided to use SHS method.

claim: The paper's uses of 'factorial' refer exclusively to the design-of-experiments sampling scheme (Central Composite Design, Box-Behnken Design) used to generate training data for the surrogates, not to a factorial crossing of surrogate class with optimizer over the optimization outcome -- confirming the audit's warned-of homonym trap.
stance_target: surface-level 'factorial' keyword matches indicate a genuine crossed surrogate x optimizer design
scope_conditions: design of experiments terminology in engineering surrogate modeling
quoted_support: Central Composite Design (CCD) is the most popular experimental design method for fitting a PR model ... It has a five-level fractional factorial designs, which is developed for fitting a second-order polynomial.

claim: The paper's uses of 'main effect' and 'interaction' refer to sensitivity analysis of the physical design variables (P1, P2, P3) on the ventilation-rate response, not to a variance decomposition of optimizer performance across surrogate model classes -- a second confirmed homonym trap.
stance_target: surface-level 'main effect'/'interaction' keyword matches indicate a genuine surrogate x optimizer ANOVA
scope_conditions: sensitivity analysis of engineering design variables
quoted_support: PR models are better suited for estimating interaction and quadratic effects of the input parameters, while Kriging-based models are better suited for identifying the main effects of the input parameters.
